doc: I52b (BUILD_PLAN §4 I52, its held-out half; whitepaper §13 'Baselines'): the held-out system of the I52 baseline protocol. Written in I52b's prereg commit, after the seal on readers lifted (I50's results recorded) and before any baseline ran on the target. Everything not stated here is I52's protocol (spec/M4/lib/I52_baselines.json, unchanged): the nine baselines and their stock modes, the scope rule, the one-core equal budget and its units, the findings schema (I52_findings.schema.json), the statuses, the span rule (matching.spans), non-vacuity and determinism. This file adds the held-out system's checkout, its labels, its budgets (a primary one by I52's rule, a secondary one fixed here) and the adjudicator's form for obligation labels. The writer had read I49's and I50's results and the target's code when writing it: every number derived from it carries that contamination caveat.

system.checkout: config/holon.json extract.sources at the key the target file names (targets/<name>/target.json checkout.config), a clone of the sealed repository at the sealed commit; never modified, every run works in a scratch copy
system.fetch_rule: Only what the seal pins: the repository at the sealed commit, and, for a baseline's build, the git submodules at the commits gitlinked in that commit's tree and the npm packages of its own lockfile (yarn.lock, --frozen-lockfile, --ignore-scripts). Each fetched submodule is recorded in the target record's scope. No other commit, branch or tag of the upstream is fetched.

labels.doc: The held-out target has no known defect: the seal forbids fetching anything of the upstream beyond the pinned commit, which is its newest tag in I49's snapshot of the refs (targets/scroll/target.json upstream.pinned_refs), so no fix commit and no defect history at the pin is available. The labels are therefore I50's preregistered rule classes (I50-P2's five rules DISCH, FACT, SORT, SYM, UNDO) instantiated as obligations on the state-moving actions of the sealed contract, the obligations HOLON's catalog would have decided had its derivation run. A label is one (rule, action) pair. Its code sites are the action's own source spans in the labelled file, as I49's extracted document records them (every src of the action's facts that lies in the labelled file: the declaration, its modifiers and the internal code the action reaches). Generated by tests_m4/_i52b.py (labels()) from that document by the rule below; never from a baseline's output.
labels.rule: Actions: every action of I49's document (gen/targets/scroll/facts/ScrollChain.extracted.json) whose own src lies in a labelled file and whose mutability is neither view nor pure, sorted by name. Rules: DISCH, FACT, SORT, SYM, UNDO in that order. Label ids O1.. numbered action-major (action 1's five rules, then action 2's, ...): the findings schema admits label ids of the forms c<nn> and O<n> only, so the held-out labels use O<n>; they name nothing of Morph's O1-O37. Anchors: the sorted distinct spans [a, b] of every src string anywhere in the action's object whose file is a labelled file ('file:a' is [a, a], 'file:a-b' is [a, b]).
labels.ground_truth: None known. A detected label is a baseline's claim, confirmed by the blinded adjudicator, that the action violates the label's obligation; it is not a verified defect. Its classification (true defect, intended asymmetry, model defect; whitepaper §13 precision) is left to I53 and recorded as unverified here.

obligations.DISCH: Dischargeability (whitepaper §5.7): every guard of the action (a require, revert, modifier or role check) can be made to hold by the principal class the action is meant for, by its own actions and time alone; a guard that only another principal or an upgrade can satisfy, or that a principal can keep false to block others, is a violation. A missing guard that lets the wrong principal take the action is also a violation.
obligations.FACT: Factorization through commitments (whitepaper §5.5): every value the action commits to (a batch hash, a data or blob hash, a state root, a public input of a proof) binds everything its consumers later rely on; two different inputs that the consumers treat differently must not yield the same commitment, and no consumed field may be left outside the commitment or the proof's public input.
obligations.SORT: Sort functoriality (whitepaper §5.6): every value keeps its type and units across the action: no narrowing cast or truncation loses a value, no signed/unsigned confusion, no reading of a field at the wrong offset or width, no conservation break (a counter, index or amount that is not preserved where it must be).
obligations.SYM: Symmetry (whitepaper §5.4): the action treats equivalent situations equally: its outcome does not depend on the timestamp, the index, which member of a role calls it or the order of two calls by different principals, except where the code's intent says so; a sentinel constant (zero or a special value) must not be confused with a real time or index.
obligations.UNDO: Undo residue (whitepaper §5.2): where the action has an inverse (add/remove, commit/revert, pause/unpause, enable/disable), performing it and then its inverse leaves no live residue: every register the pair changes is restored or never read again.

matching.location: A finding is located at label O<k> iff one of its locations names a labelled file and its line span meets one of the label's anchor spans (I52's span rule: a location span longer than 150 lines counts as its first line only). The five labels of one action share its anchors, so a finding located at one of them is located at all five.

adjudicator.doc: For every (baseline, action) with at least one located finding, one fresh tool-less process (I52_baselines.json matching.adjudicator's invocation, system prompt below) reads the frozen template spec/M4/lib/I52b_match_prompt.md filled with the action's name, the five obligations and the group's located findings (id, kind, message, locations), and answers, per rule, which finding ids claim that the action violates that rule's obligation. It never sees the baseline's name, the label ids, other systems, HOLON's outputs or I49/I50's files. One answer gives the five labels' adjudications (each with the same prompt_sha256); confirmed ids are a subset of the group's located ids; an unparsable answer gets one more attempt, then its labels count as not confirmed (recorded).
adjudicator.system_prompt: You judge whether tool findings claim that code violates a stated property. You have no tools. Answer only with what the prompt asks for.

budget.doc: I52's equal budget (one core per baseline per target, setup outside the budget and capped) at two wall clocks. The primary one is the lead's rule, I52_baselines.json holon_budget.heldout ('I50's recorded wall clock'), applied as I52 applied holon_budget.morph to M3, which recorded none: I50 recorded no wall clock in any file, so its route is measured on this machine on a scratch copy before any baseline ran, and wall_s = 60 * ceil(H / 60). The secondary one is fixed here, before any run, because the primary one is expected to be degenerate (I50's route ends at a refusal in its first step); every record and table of it is labelled secondary.

primary.wall_s_rule: 60 * ceil(H / 60), H the wall clock in seconds of I50's route measured from the committed I49 document on a scratch copy of the repository: `holon target derive --target scroll` then `holon target run --target scroll` (exits recorded; the refusal is the route's outcome), written to results/eval/heldout/holon_budget.json before any baseline result

secondary.label: secondary (larger budget, fixed at the prereg; not the lead's rule)
secondary.why: one hour per baseline, I52's setup cap: large enough that every fuzzer and symbolic executor gets minutes per unit and the reviewer can read the whole scope; it is not derived from HOLON's cost, which on this target is the primary budget

budget.agent_review: One fresh reviewer per budget, its wall clock the budget's wall_s (the system has one target), killed at it; tokens recorded, CPU null (the model provider's).

agent_review.packet: The scope files at the pinned commit, copied into a fresh /tmp directory under their repository paths, as for Morph (I52_baselines.json agent_review.stock): no renaming. Never HOLON's outputs, I49/I50's files, the labels, this file or the whitepaper.
agent_review.prompt: spec/M4/lib/I52_review_prompt.md, unchanged, filled with the packet's sorted listing and the budget's minutes
agent_review.contamination: The target is public and older than the reviewer's training data; the reviewer may have seen its code or write-ups of its audits. Its paths and identifiers are kept. Every agent number carries this caveat.

contamination: Predictions, labels and the secondary budget were written after the seal on readers lifted, by a builder who had read I49's and I50's results and the target's code. They are not blind. Every number of this iteration carries this disclosure.
